error.signature: AI gives a blanket answer on whether Colombian tap water is safe, ignoring that it varies sharply by city and department

verdict.summary: Bogota's municipal tap water (managed by EAAB) consistently scores in the 'sin riesgo' (no-risk) band of Colombia's official IRCA water-quality index and is safe to drink straight from the tap. That result does not generalize nationwide: government IRCA/DANE data shows several departments, including La Guajira and Choco, have large populations without reliable access to potable water and report high-risk or unviable IRCA scores.

dead_ends.action: Avoid all tap water in Colombia, including in Bogota, and buy bottled water everywhere as a blanket rule
dead_ends.why_fails: Bogota's water utility EAAB reports IRCA scores in the low single digits (no-risk band) under Colombia's official water-quality index, tracked by the district health observatory and the national Instituto Nacional de Salud; treating the capital the same as high-risk rural areas is an unnecessary expense and contradicts the government's own monitoring data.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That 'Latin America' or 'Colombia' as a whole is a single water-safety zone; safety in Colombia is set city-by-city and department-by-department, not nationally.

dead_ends.action: Assume that because Bogota's tap water is safe, tap water is safe everywhere in Colombia including rural areas and smaller departments
dead_ends.why_fails: DANE and Instituto Nacional de Salud data cited by Colombia's national broadcaster show several departments -- including La Guajira, where nearly half the population has limited access to continuous quality water/sanitation, and Choco, flagged at maximum alert for water-quality parameters -- fall well outside safe IRCA ranges.
dead_ends.condition: Traveling outside Bogota and other major cities with confirmed low-risk IRCA scores

workarounds.action: In Bogota (and other cities with published 'sin riesgo' IRCA scores, such as Medellin), drink tap water freely.
workarounds.how: EAAB's water is filtered, chlorinated, and monitored under WHO-aligned standards; taste (chlorine) rather than safety is the main complaint.

workarounds.action: In La Guajira, Choco, rural areas, or any department not confirmed low-risk, default to bottled or filtered water.
workarounds.how: These departments have documented IRCA high-risk or unviable ratings and populations lacking continuous potable-water access; do not extend the Bogota exception to them.
workarounds.tradeoff: Bottled/filtered water is an added cost, but the downside of ingesting contaminated water in a documented high-risk department is materially worse.
